**Dispatch order** — `domain:ui` seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. Branch: `claude/issue-6329-actionparam-one-authority`.

### The card's count is wrong, and wrong in the direction that matters

The card says `ActionParam` is "declared twice in app-shell". Measured on `origin/main` at `831be7285` with a word-boundary grep (`\bActionParam\b`, so `ActionParamDef` / `ActionParamDialog` / `ActionParamSchema` / `resolveActionParams` / `runActionParam` are excluded — a bare substring grep here returns mostly noise), it is declared **three** times:

| # | site | kind |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `packages/types/src/ui-action.ts:355` | `export interface ActionParam` — **published**, re-exported from `packages/types/src/index.ts:1023` |
| 2 | `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ActionDefaultInspector.tsx:266` | local `interface`, not exported |
| 3 | `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/ActionPreview.tsx:47` | local `interface`, not exported |

That changes the job. Ruling 甲A1 as triage quoted it — "each exported name exactly one authority" — is not asking you to pick a winner between the two local twins. **The authority already exists and is published**, with its own parity suite (`packages/types/src/__tests__/page-nav-misc-spec-parity.test.ts` and `spec-derived-unions.test.ts` both pin it against the spec's `ActionParamSchema`). The two locals are shadows of a name their own package already imports correctly: `packages/app-shell/src/utils/resolveActionParams.test.ts:21` reads `import type { ActionParam } from '@object-ui/types';`.

So the expected shape is: converge both locals onto the published type, delete both twins. Verify that framing before you act on it — if the measurement contradicts it, report rather than proceed.

### Triage's ruling, verbatim

> Inherits the 2026-08-25 family ruling 甲A1 verbatim (each component exactly one named importable author-facing type; each exported name exactly one authority): converge on one declaration, reconcile the five members against what actually flows at runtime (measure, do not pick by taste), delete the twin.

"Measure, do not pick by taste" is the binding half. The two twins are not the same shape — here they are, verbatim:

```
ActionDefaultInspector.tsx:266          ActionPreview.tsx:47
  name?: string                           name?: string
  field?: string                          field?: string
  label?: unknown                         label?: string | { en?: string }
  type?: string                           type?: string
  required?: boolean                      required?: boolean
  placeholder?: string                    options?: Array<{ label: string | { en?: string }; value: string }>
  defaultFromRow?: boolean                placeholder?: string
  [k: string]: unknown                    helpText?: string
                                          defaultValue?: unknown
                                          defaultFromRow?: boolean
```

### ⚠️ One blind instrument, called out before you write a test against it

The inspector twin carries `[k: string]: unknown`. **An index signature swallows `keyof`** — any assertion that compares a key set against that type cannot fail, because every string is already a member. If you write a pin that checks "the converged type accepts exactly these keys" and point it at a type with an index signature, it will pass whatever you do to it. Either the index signature goes away in the convergence, or your pin has to measure something else. Say in the report which of those you did, and show the pin failing before it passes.

Note also that `label?: unknown` on the inspector side is strictly weaker than the preview's `string | { en?: string }`. Converging on the published type must not silently widen either call site's runtime acceptance — check what each site actually does with `label` (`ActionPreview` has a `localize` helper right below the declaration).

### ⛔ Stop conditions — read these before you start

1. **If convergence requires adding, removing, or changing any member on the published `ActionParam` in `packages/types/src/ui-action.ts` — STOP and report.** That is a widened published surface, which is a different review tier than this card carries, and it is not yours to do inside a Task. Report the exact member and the exact call site that needs it. Deleting two local shadows is in scope; editing the published authority is not.
2. **⛔ Do not edit `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/index.ts` or `.../inspectors/index.ts`.** A sibling card (#6519) is in flight in that same `previews/` directory. Both twins are unexported locals, so deleting them should not reach either barrel; if you conclude a barrel edit is genuinely required, stop and report rather than taking it.

### File face

`ActionDefaultInspector.tsx`, `ActionPreview.tsx`, their existing test files (`ActionDefaultInspector.celGate.test.tsx`, `previews/__tests__/ActionPreview.locations.test.tsx`), plus whatever new pin you add. Reading `packages/types/src/ui-action.ts` is expected; **writing** it is stop condition 1.

### In-flight, do not touch

#6515 (`views/RecordFormPage.tsx`, `console/AppContent.tsx`) · #6519 (`views/metadata-admin/previews/object-fields-io.ts`) · #6343 (`views/InterfaceListPage.tsx`) · #6317 (`apps/site/app/components/galleryDataSource.ts`). All disjoint from your face by measurement, not by assumption.

Reverse verification is required: the pin must be written first and observed to fail against the unconverged tree, and the mutation proven on disk rather than inferred from an exit code.
